newsitem.title: UK: BT shares dip after in-line results.
newsitem.headline: BT shares dip after in-line results.

text.p: Shares in British Telecommunications Plc drifted lower in early trade on Thursday, after results in line with expectations and with attention focused mainly on its planned merger with MCI, dealers said.
The stock was down 3p at 446-1/2 by 0727 GMT -- in line with a drop in the overall market -- in thin trade of 32,996 shares.
"The results were just nothing special," said one head of equity trading.

Annual pre-tax profit rose to 3.203 billion stg in the year ended March 31, from 3.019 billion a year before. Analysts' forecasts had mostly been in a range between 3.175 billion stg and 3.224 billion stg.
Analysts said the figures were broadly in line with expectations and that prospects for BT shares were largely dependent on its transatlantic linkup with MCI.
"If you believe that the acquisition will go ahead then we are in the middle of a re-rating for BT," said Dennis Exton, analyst at Nikko Europe.
"It is a low-single digit growth company transforming itself into a mid-teens growth company, and that is the story for the next three years."

Exton said BT's results were slightly ahead of his expectations, adding that it was promising that BT continued to keep a lid on pricing pressures. He said the prospect of a 35p special dividend in September would underpin the stock in the meantime.
BT chairman Sir Iain Vallance said demand for BT's advanced products and services remained strong and the company continued to keep costs under control.

Inland call revenue was virtually unchanged but call volume grew seven percent due to 40 percent growth in ISDN calls, telemarketing services rising more than 50 percent and fixed to mobile calls rising more than 15 percent.
However,Vallance's comment that BT would attempt a legal challenge to the new Labour government's planned "windfall" tax had no effect on the shares.
